basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 2-4.' and it opens 'VERS. 2-4.-- Dixitque Abram: Domine Deus, quid dabis mihi? ego vadam absque liberis, et'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 2-4.-- Dixitque Abram: Domine Deus, quid dabis mihi? ego vadam absque liberis, et filius procuratoris domus meae iste Damascus Eliezer, et reliqua. Non quasi dubius, an fieret, de promissione Dei, cum ait: Domine Deus, quid dabis mihi? sed quomodo futurum [ Z., venturum] esset, exquirens. Sed requirendum est quis fuerit iste Eliezer Damascus, de quo dixit Abram, haeres meus erit? Ille utique fuit filius procuratoris Abrahae, qui postea, ut aiunt Hebraei, Damascum condidit, et nomen civitatis dedit regnumque in ea obtinuit. Attamen notandum, ubi nos habemus, filius procuratoris, nonnulli transtulerunt: filius Masech vernaculi mei. | Aquila vero, filius potum dantis domui meae. Theodotion, filius ejus qui super domum meam est, id est villici, qui universa dispensat, et distribuit cibaria familiae; vocaturque Damascus Eliezer. Porro Eliezer Deus meus adjutor interpretatur, qui, ut diximus, Damascum condidit. Sequitur:
